items.title: Record fundraising drive comes as food bank visits remain at historic highs in Mississauga
items.summary: Food Banks Mississauga has raised more money than ever before through its annual Thanksgiving campaign, but the record fundraising total comes as demand for food assistance continues to outpace the resources available to help residents. The organization’s 2026 Thanksgiving Drive brought in $857,029, falling short of its $900,000 goal but setting a new record for the campaign. The drive, sponsored by Keurig Dr Pepper Canada, wrapped up Tuesday (Oct. 20) as Food Banks Mississauga marked its 40th anniversary year and continued to grapple with historically high demand across the city. The organization says its network of more than 60 food programs has experienced more than half a million visits for the second consecutive year, underscoring the ongoing need for donations and community support. Food Banks Mississauga estimates that someone visits a food bank in the city every 22 seconds during the hours its network programs are open. The money raised through the Thanksgiving campaign will help keep those programs supplied with fresh and shelf-stable food, ensuring residents have access to assistance close to where they live. “People turn to food banks for all kinds of reasons: low wages, high rent, illness, disability, a job that ended,” said Meghan Nicholls, CEO of Food Banks Mississauga. “The circumstances vary, but the need is the same. ” Nicholls said community donations allow the organization to continue providing temporary relief to people experiencing food insecurity, even as the number of visits remains exceptionally high.

items.title: Loaded gun, stash of hard drugs found during car search in Mississauga
items.summary: A recent traffic stop in Mississauga’s north end for an alleged cannabis violation led police to a loaded gun, cash and other drugs that included fentanyl, heroin and crack cocaine. m. on Oct. 5 when officers with the force’s 11 Division Community Incident Response Team investigated a vehicle near Maritz Drive and Derry Road West, one block west of Hurontario Street. Police said an alleged Cannabis Control Act violation drew the officers’ attention to the vehicle. “During the investigation, officers located suspected drugs inside the vehicle,” police said in a news release, adding two suspects were subsequently arrested and charged. Following the arrests, officers searched the car and discovered a loaded 9mm Glock handgun equipped with a prohibited 15-round magazine, police said. Officers also seized more than 79 grams of suspected drugs, including fentanyl, heroin, crack cocaine and crystal methamphetamine, along with $1,260 in Canadian cash, police added.

items.title: 2,200 Mississauga Aerospace Jobs Hang on Trump's Shifting Stance Toward Bombardier
items.summary: Insauga.com reports U.S. President Donald Trump appears to be stepping back from his threat to block Bombardier aircraft sales in the United States, a shift that could ease concerns for the company's major Mississauga operations. According to the outlet, Trump signalled the change during a rally in Kansas on Monday, saying he would help the Canadian aircraft maker after learning more about its American workforce. Insauga.com reports Trump told the crowd he always viewed Bombardier as a Canadian company and added that the United States would not hurt it given its operations in Kansas, saying he would take care of those jobs. The outlet says the apparent reversal follows a September threat in which Trump declared Bombardier should no longer be allowed to sell its products in the U.S. unless it moved production there. According to insauga.com, that threat had raised concerns about the Quebec-based manufacturer's operations on both sides of the border, including its aircraft assembly centre at Toronto Pearson International Airport in Mississauga. The outlet reports the facility employs more than 2,200 people and sits on a 40-acre campus that includes a 770,000-square-foot final assembly building and a pre-flight hangar, according to the Ontario government.

items.title: Frost advisory: Environment Canada alert prompts precautionary measures for gardeners in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Take preventive measures to protect cold-sensitive plants, trees and crops, Environment Canada says. Environment and Climate Change Canada issues a frost advisory and is warning residents to cover up sensitive plants. It’s been a sunny and warm week across most of southern Ontario, but a chilly evening looms on Tuesday. Environment and Climate Change Canada has issued a yellow level frost advisory for Mississauga and Brampton, warning residents that patchy frost is expected tonight, mainly in areas away from Lake Ontario. The frost advisory extends to St. Catharines, Grimsby and Northern Niagara. According to Environment Canada, frost can potentially cause damage to plants, trees and crops. The cold temperatures impact leaves, flowers and buds still developing on stems. Gardeners can use plastic containers, sheets or bags to cover up their outdoor plants overnight.

items.title: Overnight Low of 1 C Triggers Frost Advisory Across Mississauga, Brampton and Niagara
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Environment Canada has issued a yellow frost advisory for Mississauga, Brampton and the Niagara Region, with chilly conditions expected overnight. According to the outlet, the advisory also covers St. Catharines, Grimsby, Niagara Falls and Welland, where patchy frost is expected mainly in areas away from the lakes. The outlet reports forecasters are calling for an overnight low of 1 C in Mississauga, Brampton, St. Catharines and Niagara Falls, with slightly milder conditions expected closer to the lakeshore. Environment Canada says frost at these temperatures can damage plants, trees and crops still developing leaves, flowers and buds. Insauga.com reports the cold snap is expected to break by Wednesday, with a forecast high of 16 C and sunny skies returning to the region.

items.title: Steel Shiv Fashioned From a Desk Lands Mississauga Man Another 50 Years in U.S. Terror Case
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a Mississauga man already serving time for an ISIS-inspired terror plot has been sentenced to an additional 50 years after stabbing two correctional officers inside his U.S. prison cell. According to the Justice Department, Abdulrahman El Bahnasawy, 28, received the new sentence to run consecutively to his existing 40-year term, bringing his combined sentences to 90 years. The outlet reports the attack happened in December 2020 while El Bahnasawy was serving his original sentence for plotting attacks targeting heavily populated areas of New York City. Prosecutors say he fashioned a weapon from part of a steel desk in his cell, stabbing one officer in the head and face before stabbing a second officer in the hand when she intervened. According to the Justice Department, the first officer ultimately lost his right eye from the injuries, and a pledge of allegiance to ISIS was found taped inside a locker in El Bahnasawy's cell. Insauga.com reports he pleaded guilty in November 2025 to charges including assault with intent to commit murder, possessing contraband in prison and providing material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization.

items.title: Nearly Four Years After Her Death, Hazel McCallion Still Shapes How Some Mississauga Voters Choose a Mayor
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a new survey finds some Mississauga voters are still weighing Hazel McCallion's legacy as they prepare to cast ballots in Monday's mayoral election. According to the outlet, the Liaison Strategies survey conducted earlier this month found McCallion's legacy matters to 75 per cent of residents aged 65 and older when choosing a mayor, compared with 29 per cent of those aged 18 to 34. The outlet reports McCallion built a national and international political reputation during her time as Mississauga mayor from 1978 until 2014, when she was succeeded by Bonnie Crombie, and she died in January 2023 at the age of 101. Insauga.com says that overall, regardless of age, 49 per cent of survey respondents called McCallion's legacy important, while 52 per cent said a candidate claiming to have learned from her makes no difference to their support. According to the outlet, the results are based on a random sample of 1,000 Mississauga residents surveyed Oct. 2 to 4.

items.title: Joint Business Case, Not a Construction Date, Anchors Crombie's Subway Pitch for Mississauga
items.summary: CityNews Toronto reports Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie has unveiled a plan to push for a western extension of the TTC's Line 2 subway into the city, starting with a joint business case rather than a construction commitment. According to the outlet, Crombie says she would work with the province, Metrolinx, the City of Toronto and the TTC to study extending the line west from Kipling Station through Sherway Gardens and into Mississauga's city centre. The outlet reports the proposal includes no construction timeline or cost estimate, focusing instead on determining whether the project is feasible and how it could be delivered. CityNews says Crombie, if elected, would convene meetings with government and transit partners within her first 100 days and seek federal involvement in the planning process, while also bringing a council motion in that same window to formally launch the city's participation and identify funding for its share. According to the proposal, the study would examine potential routes and station locations, including options near Sherway Gardens and City Centre, along with connections to the Hazel McCallion Line, GO Transit, MiWay and the Mississauga Transitway. The outlet reports the study would also look at ridership, travel-time savings, accessibility, nearby housing and employment growth, construction and operating costs, and environmental impacts. CityNews says Crombie wants the jointly funded study underway within her first year in office, with the initial business case completed within two years.

items.title: Bonnie Crombie says she wants to extend the Line 2 subway into Mississauga. Here is how she says she’ll do it
items.summary: Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie is laying out exactly how she plans to bring a subway extension to the city if elected. 0” transit plan, which she teased on the campaign trail last month. Her proposed plan would extend the Toronto Transit Commission’s (TTC) Line 2 west from Kipling Station, through Sherway Gardens, and into Mississauga’s city centre near the Square One Shopping Centre. In her first 100 days in office, Crombie says she would meet with officials from the Ontario government, Metrolinx (the Crown transportation corporation), the City of Toronto and the TTC to advance a joint business case for extending the line. She said those meetings will seek agreement on the study’s scope, leadership, funding and delivery schedule. ” At the same, Crombie said she’ll put forward a motion asking city council to initiate Mississauga’s participation in the business case, while directing staff to negotiate necessary partnership agreements and identify funding for the city’s share of the planning work. Within her first year in office, Crombie said, she would seek a formal partnership agreement and launch the jointly funded study of the project. Within two years, she would target completion of the initial business case and bring its findings and recommended next steps before council. Working with partners to finalize a preferred route and delivery approach, while advancing design, environment work, and funding negotiations would occupy the remainder of her four-year term, she said. “There is an appetite for this, and I haven’t heard a negative word from the province, so we are going to proceed full ahead,” Crombie said at a news conference Monday.

items.title: October 26 Marks Election Day for Mississauga's Mayor, Council and School Trustees
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents head to the polls on Monday, Oct. 26, to elect the city's next mayor, their ward and regional councillor, and local school board trustees for the 2026 to 2030 term. The city says voters can cast a ballot at any voting location within their own ward rather than being tied to a single assigned site. Officials recommend confirming you're on the voters' list before heading out, since that step can speed up the process at the polls. Anyone who received a voter notification card in September is encouraged to bring it along, though the city notes the card isn't required to vote. What is required, according to the city, is one piece of identification showing your name and a qualifying Mississauga address. The City of Mississauga says it remains committed to accessible voting, and residents looking for details on accommodations can find them through the Ways to Vote page on the city's Mississauga Votes site.
